contract.core_view: Core.view(model, { level, scope }) is pure and returns a model built with makeModel, preserving element and rel ids. level 'context' returns atLevel(model, 'context'). level 'container' returns atLevel(model, 'container'). level 'component' with no scope returns the full model minus covered rels. level 'component' with scope = a container id folds every element outside that container's subtree to its container-level ancestor, lifts rels as atLevel does, then keeps: the subtree, every element that is an endpoint of a rel touching the subtree, and the ancestors of kept elements (so the system still groups them). Covered rels are then dropped. A scope that is not a container id in the model behaves as no scope. A rel is covered when at least one of its endpoints has children and another rel links a descendant-or-self of its src to a descendant-or-self of its dst with at least one endpoint strictly deeper. This removes the container-level rollup when the component rels that make it up are visible, and keeps a component -> container rel whose provider end could not be pinned.
contract.layout_group_edges: layout(m, opts) in app.js (:727-758) gains opts.groupEdges. When it is true, rels with an endpoint that has children (and that are not structural, i.e. neither endpoint is an ancestor of the other) are returned in L.groupEdges after the groups are computed (:751-756), each resolved to { a, b } of node or group rects. They do not take part in layering. drawModel (:766-792) draws L.groupEdges with o.edgeStyle and the same edge() helper (:770-776), clipped to the rect. Groups gain a wrapping <g data-{attr}g="{id}"> so they can be double-clicked. Without opts.groupEdges, L.groupEdges is [] and the node, edge and group geometry is unchanged.
contract.state: A gains cmLevel ('container' by default), cmScope (container id | null), asbuiltFull (Core.parse of the as-built text, including components) and cdrift. loadAsbuilt (:119-124) sets asbuiltFull and keeps A.asbuilt as the container view from s2, so codemapSidebar (:855-875) and container drift are unchanged. The onFolder reset (:1117) also resets cmLevel, cmScope, asbuiltFull and cdrift, as a separate statement (see sequencing). After re-extract, the level is kept and the scope is kept if the container id still exists.
contract.navigation: The cm-bar (:895-899) gets a segmented control Context · Containers · Components (data-a="cmlevel" data-level=...), with the current one pressed. Components is disabled, with a title 'No components were found', when asbuiltFull has no component elements. When scoped, a breadcrumb 'All ▸ <container>' follows: 'All' goes to unscoped Components. A dblclick on a container node at Containers level, or on a group at Components level, sets level 'component' and scope to that container. A dblclick on a component node selects it. A dblclick on empty canvas, or Backspace while the Code map is active and focus is not in an input, textarea, select, contenteditable or .monaco-editor, goes up: scoped or unscoped Components goes to Containers, Containers goes to Context, and Context does nothing. Every level or scope change sets cmZoom to 'fit', keeps cmSel if that id exists in the new view (otherwise clears it), and redraws. Existing click behaviour (:1025-1026) is unchanged.
contract.drift_components: Core.driftComponents(design, built) takes the full design and full as-built models. It first maps containers with driftModels(atLevel(design, 'container'), atLevel(built, 'container')); atLevel keeps ids, so the mapping applies to the full models. A built container is scored when its design match has component children. In a scored container, built components match design components of the matched container by key(name) or d.aka (core.js:394-397 key and get). Unmatched built components go to unknownEls, and design components with no built match go to missingEls. Components of unscored containers go into neutral. Rel status is computed for every built rel with a component endpoint. First map each endpoint: a matched component maps to its design component; a component of an unscored container maps to its container's design match; a non-component end maps via the container mapping. The status is then decided by the first rule that applies. (1) An unmapped end makes the rel 'unmapped'. (2) Both ends mapping to one design element, or an intra-container rel of an unscored container, makes it 'neutral'. (3) An intra-container rel in a scored container is 'matched' only if the design has exactly that component rel, and otherwise is 'undeclared'. (4) A cross-container rel is 'matched' if the design has the rel between the mapped ends, or between their container-level ancestors, and otherwise is 'undeclared'. unrealised lists design rels with both ends mapped to components that no built component rel matched. The return value is { toDesign, toBuilt, relStatus, undeclared, unrealised, unknownEls, missingEls, neutral: Set<built id>, scored: Set<built container id>, adoptable: [{ built: container id, design: design container id }] }, where adoptable holds unscored built containers that have components and a design match. It is computed in recompile (:125-131) as A.cdrift when A.asbuiltFull and A.model.elements.size are set.
contract.splice: Core.spliceComponents(designText, design, designContainerId, built, builtContainerId) returns { text } or { error }. It is pure and makes no other edits. It errors when: the design element is not a container; it already has children; its declaration line (el.line) doesn't contain the container keyword; or its block can't be located by brace matching (ignoring braces inside strings) from that line. Otherwise it inserts, one indent level deeper than the container line: one '<ident> = component "Name" "" "tech"' line per built component of the built container, then one one-line relationship per built rel between two of those components, written in the dsl.js form '<a> -> <b> "label" "tech" { properties { "d.interaction" "sync|async" } }'. Cross-container rels are not written; the design keeps them at container level. A container without a block gets ' {' appended to its line and a closing '}' line. Idents reuse the built ident, suffixed _2 and up on collision with an existing design ident. The result parses with no new errors, and every original line is unchanged except the container line when ' {' is appended. Adopted intra-container sync rels are ordinary sync rels to the compiler. DC003 counts them as hops (core.js:281, structural only exempts ancestor/descendant pairs), so a long in-process chain can raise a DC003 warning. This is accepted and documented under Known limitations, because a new d.* property would be DC000 (core.js:212) and changing DC003 is out of scope.
